correctness.rationale: The two-edge rainbow criterion is equivalent to having no repeated binary row or column signatures. Minimizing the weights of distinct length-v signatures gives the exact budget; when u=v, v−1 selected unit signatures distinguish all columns, and when u≥v+1, all v units are selected. These cases show constraints on the other side introduce no gap. The optimizer count follows by choosing the terminal layer and permuting the u signatures. Partition-lattice Möbius inversion counts every permissible binary matrix by the number of 1 entries. Complementation proves reciprocity. The packaged brute-force graph-check script independently passes nine minimum/count and six polynomial-comparison cases.

The 2018 color-code study establishes the underlying signature method, but the full red-edge extremum, classification, and Möbius weight polynomial are not stated or implied by the inspected results. value.rationale: An exact designated-color budget and complete labeled optimizer classification are motivated by sparse two-color rainbow connectivity in complete bipartite graphs, and are different mathematical information from the established existence threshold. The complete red-edge distribution is also supplied through a closed finite partition sum, with no arbitrary small-order restriction. The solution addresses a natural two-parameter optimization and enumeration task with a nontrivial equal-part boundary.
